_scope_note: The defect is in the harness's connection lifecycle, not in any test's assertions and not in any product code. All 346 packages/db tests PASS at base_sha; the suite fails only on 2 unhandled pool errors. packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts is deliberately NOT in scope: its DD29-3 test already closes its own client and calls ctx.teardown() in a finally block, and the leaked connection is owned by the harness. If the writer proves the leak originates in the test file rather than the harness, that is a scope finding - report it, do not widen the diff. The slice doc and this manifest are in scope on purpose (AP-39/AP-40 lesson).
negative_scope: NEVER attach a blanket, always-on error swallow to any pool or client. The handler must suppress ONLY during teardown and ONLY for the known connection-termination codes; outside that window every error must still surface. A harness that cannot report a connection failure is the 'gate that cannot fail' this kit already recorded once - see scope-gate v14's own header note on autopilot-backlog-reconcile.

NEVER remove or weaken `WITH (FORCE)` on the teardown DROP DATABASE. It exists because closing connections alone leaves the database, the cluster-global ownerRole and its job_definer membership behind - a LOGIN role with a fixed password and BYPASSRLS-via-membership on a shared cluster (codex round-07 [P1], recorded in the teardown's own comment). Terminating stragglers is the point; delivering FATAL to a listener-less pool is the defect.

NEVER set fileParallelism:false in packages/db/vitest.config.* to make the symptom go away. Serial execution was deliberately re-enabled to parallel after both original hazards were closed, with >=5 consecutive green full-suite runs as evidence. Hiding a lifecycle bug behind serialisation trades a 90s suite for a slower one and leaves the leak live.
NO change to any test assertion, expected count, or migration. 346 tests pass at base_sha and must still pass at the same count.
NO change to product code under packages/db/src outside test-harness.ts.

_measured_defect.measured_at: 2026-08-10, CI run #223 job verify (also #224), step Test
_measured_defect.symptom: Test Files 5 passed (5) / Tests 346 passed (346) / Errors 2 errors / Failed
_measured_defect.error: Postgres FATAL 57P01 (admin_shutdown), routine ProcessInterrupts, on a connection with user '<dbName>_owner' to database '<dbName>' - measured instance: plexco_migrate_dd29_upgrade
_measured_defect.originating_file: packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts, last test before the throw: 'DD29-3 A1/A3: old plans rows survive alongside the new ones, and a pre-existing free_web row remaps to free at version 1'
_measured_defect.mechanism: teardown() ends ownerPool and every workerPool, then runs DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE). Since PostgreSQL 13 FORCE terminates every remaining connection to the target database, and a terminated backend reports 57P01 to its client. A pg.Pool with no 'error' listener turns that into an unhandled error, which vitest counts under 'Errors' and which fails the suite even though no test failed.
_measured_defect.why_it_survived: Reproduces on CI, not on the owner's machine (683/732 green locally) - a timing-dependent race. docs/autopilot-backlog.md task deps-security-bump already recorded '2x Postgres 57P01' as infrastructure interruptions in late July; it was classified as noise and no task was opened. It has since become a permanent red.

_leak_hypotheses: H1 - listener-less pools. grep '\.on(.error.' packages/db/src/test-harness.ts returns ZERO matches across 8 pool/client construction sites. node-postgres documents that a Pool without an 'error' listener will surface idle-client errors as unhandled. This alone explains 'Errors 2' with 0 test failures and is the cheapest fix.

H2 - a connection teardown() does not know about. The error's user is '<dbName>_owner', i.e. ownerPool or a workerPool, both of which teardown() ends BEFORE the DROP. pg.Pool.end() resolves once idle clients are closed; a client still checked out at that moment is not waited on. Worth measuring - a leak that H1 merely silences is still a leak.
_leak_hypotheses._note: H1 and H2 are not alternatives. H1 stops the suite failing; H2 is whether anything is actually still connected. The writer must report which one the evidence supports rather than fixing H1 and declaring the matter closed.

security_review.reason: Test-harness connection lifecycle only. No product code, no auth/permission path, no migration, no external input, no deployment surface. The one security-adjacent element - the teardown DROP ROLE that removes a fixed-password LOGIN role with BYPASSRLS-via-membership from a shared cluster - is explicitly protected by negative_scope and must come out unchanged.
